review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked closely at the two boundary-leg theorems (boundBridge_legM and boundBridge_legN), the in-left and in-right slot conditions (powSplit_cond_left and powSplit_cond_right), and the two section/retraction proofs. I confirmed the line ranges and the duplicated blocks with Read and Grep. I did not read the definitions of modPowLegM, modPowGlue and midConcatFst in PowChain.lean, so the exact shape of the proposed shared lemmas is a sketch that has not been compiled. The remaining proofs (headMod_act, powSplit_powMulDesc and so on) are not duplicated nontrivial reasoning. powSplit_powMulDesc and powMulDesc_powSplit are only superficially similar, so I did not report them.

findings.problem: The two theorems repeat the same proof skeleton. Both obtain `hsplit` from `concat_split_bound`. Both prove `sub1`, which is `whiskerLeft_comp_tensorHom` applied to `(powPeel X b).inv`. Both introduce about a dozen `set` abbreviations. Both then run a hand-written `calc` of about 25 steps that only moves `Category.assoc` and `congrArg` around. In that calc the same prefix is derived twice: modPowLegM/N = w₁ ≫ w₂ ≫ cc, then `E1` turns `cc ≫ cs ≫ ci ≫ ππ ≫ mT` into `pd ≫ pl ≫ ππ ≫ mT`, then `hM`/`hN` is applied. The tail `(σ₁ ≫ σ₂ ≫ σ₃ ≫ bA ≫ tH)` regrouping into `boundBridge` is repeated as well. Only the window map (`actRight A X ▷ X` versus `(α_ X A X).hom ≫ (X ◁ actLeft A X)`) and the final leg computation (`E2`) differ. Any change to the bridge or to `concat_split_bound` has to be made in two places of about 150 lines each.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma for an arbitrary window map `w : (X ⊗ A) ⊗ X ⟶ X ⊗ X`. It says: `((tensorPow D X a ◁ w) ▷ tensorPow D X b) ≫ ((α_ (tensorPow D X a) X X).inv ▷ tensorPow D X b) ≫ powDetach X (a+1) b ≫ (tensorPow D X (a+1) ◁ (powPeel X b).inv) ≫ (modPowπ A X (a+1) ⊗ₘ modPowπ A X (b+1)) ≫ mT` is equal to `((tensorPow D X a ◁ w) ▷ tensorPow D X b) ≫ modPowGlue … ≫ cs ≫ ci ≫ ππ ≫ mT`. Proof sketch: `reassoc_of% (concat_split_bound X a b)`, plus `whiskerLeft_comp_tensorHom` to rewrite `pl ≫ ππ` as `modPowπ ⊗ₘ headMod`. Add a second small lemma saying that `pl ≫ ππ ≫ mT = (modPowπ A X (a+1) ⊗ₘ headMod A X b) ≫ mT`. Then `boundBridge_legM` is `rw [this lemma, reassoc_of% hM]` followed by `sub2`, and `boundBridge_legN` is `rw [this lemma, reassoc_of% hN]` followed by `n2`–`n5`. The two `calc` blocks can then be replaced by `simp only [Category.assoc]` and `rw`, with `reassoc_of%` supplying the associativity. No new hypotheses are needed beyond those already on the two theorems.
findings.benefit: This removes roughly 200 lines of mechanical associativity bookkeeping. The shared reduction through the split concatenation is proved and named once. A reader sees only the genuinely different content, which is the M-leg absorption by `modPowπ_actRight` and the N-leg absorption by `headMod_act`. Changes to `boundBridge` or the split then need no parallel edits.

findings.problem: The two theorems have the same structure. Each proves a `hc2` that turns `concat ≫ powCast ≫ concat⁻¹` into a whiskered `powCast` using `hwrc`/`hwlc`, `Iso.hom_inv_id` and `comp_id`. Each sets `ci`, `ππ` and `mT`. Each proves a `key : ∀ w, …` by a 5–6 step `calc` with the same moves. It splits the cast with `powCast_comp_assoc`, rewrites with the `modPowLeg_concat_fst`/`snd` result `hM1`, applies `hc2`, and ends with `whiskerRight_tensorHom` or `whiskerLeft_comp_tensorHom`. Each then closes with `Iso.cancel_iso_hom_left`, `key (winLegM A X)`, `key (winLegN A X)` and `congrArg … (modPow_rel …)`. The only differences are which side the concatenation acts on and which tensor-hom absorption lemma is used. The ten-line `calc` terms with large repeated expressions are hard to read and easy to break.
findings.proposed_change: Prove one lemma on arbitrary slot data. For example, given `hc2` in the form `(tensorPowConcat X p q).hom ≫ powCast X h ≫ (tensorPowConcat X (a+1) (b+1)).inv = c`, show `Q ≫ (tensorPowConcat X p q).hom ≫ powCast X h ≫ ci ≫ ππ ≫ mT = Q ≫ c ≫ ππ ≫ mT`. Prove it with `reassoc_of% hc2`, and use `powCast_comp` to merge the two casts. Then state `key` once per side as `simp`/`rw` with `reassoc_of% hM1`, `reassoc_of% hc2`, `whiskerRight_tensorHom` (resp. `whiskerLeft_comp_tensorHom`) and `Category.assoc`. Pull the common closing step into a lemma that takes `key`, the relation `modPow_rel` and the iso cancellation. This gives `powSplit_cond_left` and `powSplit_cond_right` as two short instantiations (for example, by `Iso.cancel_iso_hom_left` and `congrArg`), using their existing hypotheses `hL`, `hR` and the same instances.
findings.benefit: The roughly 240 lines of near-duplicate calc steps shrink to a few lines per theorem. The structural reason both cases work becomes visible: the cast and concat identity, then the tensor-hom absorption, then `modPow_rel`. Future changes to `modPowGlue` or the cast conventions need only one proof update.
